reasoning:
To find the characteristic polynomial of a matrix $ A $, we compute the determinant of $ \lambda I - A $, where $ I $ is the identity matrix and $ \lambda $ is a scalar. This polynomial is defined as:

$$
\text{det}(\lambda I - A)
$$

Given the matrix:

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix}
-4 & -13 & 10 \\
-9 & 10 & 4 \\
12 & -5 & -14
\end{pmatrix}
$$

We form the matrix $ \lambda I - A $:

$$
\lambda I - A = \begin{pmatrix}
\lambda + 4 & 13 & -10 \\
9 & \lambda - 10 & -4 \\
-12 & 5 & \lambda + 14
\end{pmatrix}
$$

The determinant of this matrix is calculated using cofactor expansion. Expanding along the first row, we compute the determinant as:

$$
(\lambda + 4)\left[(\lambda - 10)(\lambda + 14) - (-4)(5)\right] - 13\left[9(\lambda + 14) - (-4)(-12)\right] + (-10)\left[9(5) - (\lambda - 10)(-12)\right]
$$

After simplifying each term and combining like terms, the result is:

$$
\lambda^3 + 8\lambda^2 - 341\lambda - 744
$$

This is the characteristic polynomial of the matrix.
